issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent between the problem statement / solution and the template. The UML and the solution define Meal(String, String[]) (name first, then ingredients), but the template's Meal constructor is declared as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). Additionally, the template's Main uses new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...}) (name first), which will not match the template Meal constructor. This mismatch will cause compilation errors and confuse students about the intended constructor signature.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so it matches the UML in the problem statement and the solution. Update any template usages (e.g., Main) if necessary. This will align the template with the specified design and avoid compilation errors for students.

issues.description: Constructor parameter ordering for Meal is inconsistent between the problem statement / solution and the template. The problem diagram and the solution use Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first, then ingredients), and example usage in the problem/Main assumes that order (e.g., new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})). The template's Meal constructor is declared as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first, then name). This mismatch breaks the direct mapping from the problem to the provided starter code, can cause compile errors when students try the example, and forces them to resolve an unexpected API difference instead of focusing on the exercise learning goals.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the template Meal constructor with the problem description and solution by changing its signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first, then ingredients). Alternatively, if the reversed order is intentional, update the problem statement/examples to use the template's parameter order — but aligning the template to the documented/example API is the least confusing fix for students.
